title: High Quality Genomic DNA Extraction from Gram-Negative Bacteria
author: G-Biosciences
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.e56bg9e
materials: Allow the sample to cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Add culture to tube
steps.instruction: Pipette 0.5 ml of an overnight Gram‑negative bacterial culture into a 1.5 ml micro‑fuge tube.

steps.title: Resuspend cells by vortex
steps.instruction: Vortex the tube briefly to resuspend any cells remaining in the residual supernatant.

steps.title: Pellet cells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 2–3 minutes to pellet the cells.

steps.title: Discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully remove and discard the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet.

steps.title: Add Lysis Buffer and mix
steps.instruction: Add 700 µl Lysis Buffer to the pellet and mix by inverting the tube a few times.

steps.title: Incubate for lysis
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 55–60 °C for 15 minutes (do not exceed 60 °C).

steps.title: Optional Proteinase K digestion
steps.instruction: If desired, add 1 µl Proteinase K per 100 µl Lysis Buffer, then incubate at 60 °C for 1–2 hours, inverting the tube periodically each hour.

steps.title: Add chloroform and mix
steps.instruction: Add 200 µl chloroform and mix by inverting the tube several times.

steps.title: Phase separation centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 14,000 × g and carefully transfer the upper aqueous phase to a clean micro‑centrifuge tube.

steps.title: Transfer aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Move the collected upper phase to a new clean tube for downstream processing.

steps.title: Add DNA Stripping Solution
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl DNA Stripping Solution to the tube and invert several times to mix.

steps.title: Incubate DNA stripping
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture for 5–10 minutes at 60 °C.

steps.title: Add Precipitation Solution
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl Precipitation Solution and invert several times; if a white precipitate does not appear, add 50 µl aliquots of Precipitation Solution until it does.

steps.title: Centrifuge to collect precipitate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample at 14,000 × g for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Isopropanol DNA precipitation
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a clean tube and add 500 µl isopropanol to precipitate the genomic DNA.

steps.title: Optional glycogen carrier addition
steps.instruction: If desired, add 2 µl Mussel Glycogen as a DNA carrier before the next centrifugation step.

steps.title: Pellet DNA by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Invert the tubes 10 times to mix, then centrifuge at 14,000 × g for 5 minutes to pellet the genomic DNA.

steps.title: Remove ethanol supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully discard the supernatant, leaving the DNA pellet behind.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 70% ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 700 µl 70 % ethanol to the tube and invert several times to wash the DNA pellet.

steps.title: Centrifuge ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 1 minute at 14,000 × g.

steps.title: Remove ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Decant or pipette off the ethanol wash completely.

steps.title: Dry pellet briefly
steps.instruction: Invert the tube on a clean absorbent surface for several minutes to allow excess ethanol to drain; do not let the pellet dry completely.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA in TE Buffer
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl TE Buffer to the pellet.

steps.title: Rehydrate DNA at room temperature
steps.instruction: Incubate at room temperature for at least 15 minutes to rehydrate the DNA (alternatively, incubate at 55–60 °C for 5–60 minutes to speed rehydration).

steps.title: Optional RNase treatment
steps.instruction: Add 1 µl LongLife™ RNase per 100 µl TE Buffer if RNA removal is desired.

steps.title: Store DNA and record yield
steps.instruction: Store the DNA at 4 °C for short‑term use; for long‑term storage keep at –20 °C or –80 °C. Typical yield: 30–80 µg DNA per 1 ml Gram‑negative bacteria.
